questions.stem: The definition of democracy as "government of the people, by the people, for the people" is credited to

options.text: Abraham Lincoln
Baron de Montesquieu
A. V. Dicey
Max Weber

questions.explanation: Abraham Lincoln used the phrase in the Gettysburg Address of 1863. It captures three ideas at once: the people are the source of authority, they choose their rulers, and government must serve their interest.

distractorRationale.b: Montesquieu is associated with the doctrine of separation of powers
distractorRationale.c: Dicey is associated with the principles of the rule of law
distractorRationale.d: Weber is associated with the classification of authority into traditional, charismatic and legal-rational

options.text: citizens assemble in the market square to pass laws themselves
citizens elect representatives who make laws on their behalf
the President appoints all members of the National Assembly
traditional rulers decide policy for their communities

questions.explanation: In a large state it is impossible for two hundred million people to legislate in person, so citizens transfer that task to elected senators and representatives. Government by chosen representatives is what indirect or representative democracy means.

distractorRationale.a: That describes direct democracy, as practised in ancient Athens
distractorRationale.c: Appointment by the President would destroy the electoral basis of representation
distractorRationale.d: Traditional rulers advise and influence but hold no legislative power under the 1999 Constitution

questions.stem: The principle that every qualified adult citizen is entitled to one vote of equal value is called

options.text: separation of powers
universal adult suffrage
collective responsibility
judicial review

questions.explanation: Universal adult suffrage means the right to vote is not restricted by sex, wealth, education, religion or ethnicity, only by a minimum age — 18 years in Nigeria. It is the practical expression of political equality.

distractorRationale.a: Separation of powers concerns the division of functions among the organs of government
distractorRationale.c: Collective responsibility is a feature of cabinet government
distractorRationale.d: Judicial review is the power of courts to test the validity of laws and official acts

questions.stem: Which device allows a modern state to obtain a direct decision from the whole electorate on a single issue?

options.text: A referendum
A vote of no confidence
A public hearing of a legislative committee
A census

questions.explanation: A referendum, or plebiscite, puts one question directly to the voters, so it is a surviving element of direct democracy inside a representative system. The recall and the initiative work in a similar way.

distractorRationale.b: A vote of no confidence is taken by legislators, not by the electorate
distractorRationale.c: A public hearing gathers views but takes no binding decision from the voters
distractorRationale.d: A census counts the population; it decides nothing

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of democratic government?

options.text: It permits the peaceful change of government
Decision making can be slow because of consultation and debate
It protects the fundamental rights of citizens
It makes rulers accountable to the electorate

questions.explanation: The very consultation that makes democracy legitimate also makes it slow, since bills must pass committees, both chambers and public hearings. In an emergency this deliberateness can be a real cost.

distractorRationale.a: Peaceful transfer of power is one of democracy's chief advantages
distractorRationale.c: Protection of rights is an advantage, not a drawback
distractorRationale.d: Accountability is the central merit of democratic rule

questions.stem: A country holds elections every four years, but opposition rallies are banned, the courts take instructions from the executive and only the state broadcaster may report results. The country is best described as

options.text: a full democracy, because elections are held regularly
undemocratic, because the other principles of democracy are absent
a direct democracy, because voters decide personally
a confederation, because power is decentralised

questions.explanation: Elections are a necessary but not a sufficient condition for democracy. Where freedom of association, judicial independence and press freedom are missing, the vote cannot express the genuine will of the people, so the election becomes a formality rather than a choice.

distractorRationale.a: This mistakes one principle for the whole set; regular elections can coexist with authoritarian rule
distractorRationale.c: Direct democracy means citizens legislate in person, which is not described here
distractorRationale.d: A confederation concerns the distribution of power between a centre and its units, a separate question

questions.stem: Majority rule in a democracy entitles the winning majority to remove the political rights of the minority.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Democracy is majority rule with minority rights: the majority governs, but the minority keeps its rights to speak, organise, litigate and contest the next election. Stripping those rights produces the tyranny of the majority, which is a failure of democracy rather than an exercise of it.

distractorRationale.a: This reading makes each election final and permanent, which would destroy the possibility of peaceful change

questions.stem: Direct democracy is impracticable in a modern state such as Nigeria mainly because of

options.text: the absence of a written constitution
the large size of the population and territory
the existence of more than one political party
the shortage of qualified lawyers

questions.explanation: Direct democracy requires all citizens to assemble and decide in person, which was feasible in a small Greek city-state but impossible for over two hundred million people spread across 36 states. Scale is why representation was invented.

distractorRationale.a: Nigeria has a written constitution, and having one would not make mass assembly possible anyway
distractorRationale.c: Multiple parties are a feature of representative democracy, not an obstacle to direct rule
distractorRationale.d: Legal expertise is irrelevant to whether citizens can physically assemble to legislate
